# tasks

<!-- ops:identity start — generated by ops-docs; edit identity.toml -->
*The file-based task tracker every project here uses*

Tracks work as Markdown records for people and coding agents, with records in-tree,
linked to a code checkout, or detached in a records repository. One Rust CLI validates
writes and answers in JSON; shipped skills teach the session protocol. A host registry
supports reading across projects.

Authority: `docs/task-model.md`
<!-- ops:identity end -->

## Install

<a id="quick-start"></a>

### 1. Install

With a Rust toolchain and just:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/khughitt/tasks ~/.local/src/tasks
cd ~/.local/src/tasks
just setup
just install
just install-skills
```

The binary has no service dependency. `just install` runs `cargo install --locked --path .` with checked dependency versions.
`install-skills` links each shipped skill into `~/.claude/skills` and
`~/.agents/skills`. A pinned per-project setup keeps a full checkout at the desired
revision and links the selected skill from the project's .claude/skills/:

```sh
mkdir -p <project>/.claude/skills
ln -s <absolute-pinned-checkout>/skills/tasks <project>/.claude/skills/tasks
```

Keep that checkout and its documentation available: relative contract links resolve
through the skill link into the checkout. Reinstall the binary with `just install` after CLI changes.

### 2. Initialize a project

```sh
cd <project>
tasks init --prefix demo
```

A prefix is a letter followed by one to seven lowercase letters/digits. Init
creates task records and document roots and registers the project on this host.
For existing records, custom roots, linked or detached storage, read
[project adoption](docs/project-operations.md#layout-and-adoption) first.

### 3. Tell the project's agents

Add to the project's `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`:

```text
Work is tracked with tasks; follow the tasks skill (skills/tasks/SKILL.md in
its installed location). Adopt its process and workspace policy: the task's
process field decides whether design and planning run.
```

## Usage

```sh
tasks add "Emit rows" -p 1 --size s --complexity low --process direct
tasks prime                      # session context and available work
tasks ready                      # actionable todo leaves
tasks tree                       # containment hierarchy
tasks start <id>                 # claim before work
tasks note <id> "<evidence>"
tasks park <id> "<next action>"   # releases claim, keeps status
tasks done <id> "<result>"
tasks check
```

Use returned ids. Prefer CLI writes to editing records. JSON is the automation
contract; add `--pretty` for human output, and inspect warnings on success.
`tasks --help` and `tasks <command> --help` list all flags. The
[user guide](docs/user-guide.md) explains statuses, goals, review, shelves,
recurrence, filters, blockers and bounded summaries. The
[ownership protocol](docs/ownership.md) defines claims, identity and safe release.

The shipped [tasks](skills/tasks/SKILL.md), [curate](skills/curate/SKILL.md) and
[scope](skills/scope/SKILL.md) skills cover session work, bounded maintenance and
idea review. Report tool observations with
`tasks feedback --project <prefix> "<title>" --category friction|gap|idea|positive`.

## Configuration

Project settings live in the records directory's tasks/.config.toml. Host
registry and settings are under `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/tasks` or `~/.config/tasks`;
claims and parks are host-local state. See [configuration](docs/configuration.md)
for every accepted key, default, environment override and validation rule.
Color is opt-in for pretty output; JSON remains unstyled.

## Layout

- `src/`, `tests/`: CLI implementation and isolated fixtures.
- `skills/`: agent procedures shipped with the binary's repository.
- `docs/`: current public contracts and operating guides.
- `identity.toml`, `tools/`: identity, adopted guild contract, shared checks and
  CLI vocabulary, plus supported review/wait backfill tools.
- Project records: `tasks/<id>.md`, `tasks/files/<id>/`, and working documents,
  either in-tree or in the linked/detached records home. `tasks where` explains it.

| How is retained custody observed or transferred? | [Retention](docs/retention.md) |

Completed retained history survives project rename through verified Git-anchored
lineage; pending operations still block it. See [retention](docs/retention.md#project-rename-and-historical-locators)
for source-proof, historical-query and coordinated-reader rollout requirements.

Public references describe current behavior. Historical designs, plans and notes
are kept in private project records and are not required to use the public tool.
This repository's local `tasks check` hygiene requires those private records.

For development run `just setup`, then focused checks through
`just test-one <name>` or `just test-one --test cli <name>`, and
`just check-hygiene` before committing. `just ci-check-hygiene` is the portable
subset for a public clone. Never invoke cargo test directly: recipes isolate
Git fixtures and record timing. The checked `.tt.toml` disables automatic broad
local runs; `just test-full` deliberately forces the full suite. Branch pushes
run forced broad checks/full tests in CI; no push or CI result is implied by a
local policy skip. [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) has the full contributor gate policy.
